articles.title: Construction Industry Still Faces Challenges Regarding Foundation Design in Chalk Strata
articles.excerpt: At an annual lecture hosted by the British Geotechnical Association, experts emphasized that the construction sector still has significant lessons to learn regarding the influence of chalk strata on foundation design and construction, noting that overlooked geological risks lead to cost overruns.
articles.content: The UK built environment sector continues to encounter significant challenges regarding how chalk strata influence foundation design and construction processes. During an annual lecture hosted by the British Geotechnical Association, geotechnical specialist Chris Raison shared insights derived from nearly forty years of professional experience on projects associated with chalk bedrock. Despite decades of published guidance and research, the industry regularly faces disputes and claims concerning chalk foundations. The core issue is frequently not chalk as an inherent engineering problem, but rather the absence of chalk or modifications to the material resulting from natural or anthropogenic processes. Weathering processes can diminish the density, strength, and stiffness of chalk, while dissolution features generate weak zones that remain difficult to assess accurately. Examining case studies from projects undertaken between 1987 and 2022, the lecture demonstrated how geological and geotechnical risks directly impact the construction and long-term performance of pile foundations. Despite a substantial body of existing technical literature, these lessons are not consistently applied across the industry, and a failure to thoroughly understand site-specific ground conditions frequently results in project delays and increased costs.
articles.originalTitle: Industry still has lessons to learn about chalk foundations - New Civil Engineer

articles.title: Exhibition at Gagosian Gallery in London Examines René Magritte's Works and Psychoanalytic Critique
articles.excerpt: An exhibition at the Gagosian Gallery in London brings together works by Belgian surrealist René Magritte, featuring his clever conundrums, cloud paintings, and lesser-known pieces from his deliberately provocative 'Vache' period.
articles.content: The Gagosian Gallery in London is hosting a notable exhibition focused on the works of Belgian surrealist artist René Magritte. The presentation highlights the artist's complex compositions that playfully satirize logical forms and psychoanalytic interpretations. Included in the selection are cloud and sky paintings that, despite their innocent appearance, demonstrate subtle observation and nuanced technique. The exhibition also features works reflecting Magritte's critique of Sigmund Freud's symbol analyses, alongside pieces like The Interpretation of Dreams, lent by artist Jasper Johns, which questions the boundaries between dreams and reality. Furthermore, the display includes examples from Magritte's provocative 'Vache' period, during which he deliberately produced deliberately clumsy paintings to challenge conventional expectations. The exhibition offers a detailed look into the artist's subversive approach to representation and established artistic norms.
articles.originalTitle: Magritte: This Is Still Not a Pipe review – brilliance and trash from the surrealist who sent up Freud - The Guardian

articles.title: American Society of Civil Engineers Launches New Certification Standard for Project Utility Engineering
articles.excerpt: The American Society of Civil Engineering and Civil Engineering Certification have launched a new certification program allowing experienced professionals to demonstrate their expertise in project utility engineering.
articles.content: The American Society of Civil Engineers and Civil Engineering Certification have introduced a new credential aimed at project utility engineering professionals seeking to demonstrate their expertise. Industry leaders noted that the framework establishes a definitive benchmark for the discipline, which remains in its early stages of development. The credential provides a structured roadmap regarding required knowledge, operational activities, and project responsibilities. Candidates must possess a professional license and at least a decade of relevant experience, while engineers from jurisdictions without such licensing requirements must demonstrate fifteen years of total practice. The evaluation process involves an application review by an industry board followed by an online examination. Developed through extensive subject matter contributions, the program encompasses six core domains, including asset management, utility coordination, mapping, and industry standards. Issuing organizations indicate that widespread adoption of these standards will optimize utility governance, mitigate project delays, minimize financial overruns, and enhance the overall efficiency of civil infrastructure development across the sector.
articles.originalTitle: BC.PUE certification: Setting a new standard for project utility engineering - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)

articles.title: Vogue World Milan Finale Features Thousands of Handcrafted Paper Objects
articles.excerpt: The grand finale of Vogue World Milan featured over six thousand handcrafted paper objects released from the Galleria dome, designed by Jony Ive's creative studio.
articles.content: The grand finale of the Vogue World event in Milan featured a constellation of over six thousand paper objects released from the ceiling of the Galleria. Conceived through a prolonged design process by a creative studio, the installation honored the manufacturing heritage of Milan. Drawing inspiration from natural forms, Venetian mosaics, and local lace traditions, the objects were folded entirely by hand from single sheets of paper without the use of adhesive. The team engineered digital simulations and conducted physical aerodynamic tests in various environments to observe how the objects would disperse through the architectural space. Developed with an emphasis on dynamic movement rather than simple descent, the paper elements were designed to mimic natural intelligence in motion. The objects also served as physical keepsakes for attendees, featuring inscribed details noting their origin and the time and location of the event.

articles.content: The Crystal Bridges Museum has announced Brooklyn-based artist, photographer, and filmmaker Tyler Mitchell as the recipient of the 2026 Don Tyson Prize for the Advancement of American Art. Formerly a biennial award, the prize has transitioned to an annual cycle with a cash award of $250,000, recognizing living individuals or institutions that have transformed how American art is experienced and understood. Rod Bigelow, executive director of Crystal Bridges, noted that Mitchell has generated experiences extending well beyond traditional museum spaces through photography, film, publishing, and fashion. In 2018, he achieved historic recognition as the first Black artist to photograph the cover of American Vogue.

articles.title: How Touchscreens and Digital Networks Are Shaping the Future of Contemporary Art
articles.excerpt: Artist John Gerrard examines real-time virtual simulations built using game engines and explores the expanding potential of digital touchscreens within contemporary art, addressing the intersection of digital networks and physical spaces.
articles.content: Artist John Gerrard develops real-time virtual simulations centered on themes of energy, ecology, and power through the application of game-engine technology. His software-based projects, featured on digital platforms such as the Los Angeles County Museum of Art website, utilize scanned objects to invite viewers to engage with variable narratives via touchscreen interfaces. According to the artist, mobile devices and networked platforms offer the capacity to generate three-dimensional image objects that extend beyond conventional two-dimensional media consumption. Blockchain-based art tokens provide a formal structuring mechanism for the provenance, documentation, and collection of digital artworks. Despite the integration of artificial intelligence agents, human labor and iterative coding remain central to achieving the desired perceptual qualities within the work. The evolving relationship between digital practices and physical exhibition spaces prompts commercial galleries and institutions to adapt to new modes of cultural participation. Through ongoing institutional involvement and public presentations, these virtual environments reach diverse audiences, pointing toward an artistic landscape where physical gatherings and fluid digital networks coexist within contemporary culture.

articles.title: Skanska to Lead Major Rehabilitation of Historic Potomac River Bridge
articles.excerpt: The 1950-built Potomac River bridge in the Washington, D.C. area is undergoing rehabilitation through a design-build project led by Skanska USA Civil.
articles.content: A comprehensive rehabilitation process is underway for the nearly half-mile-long, four-lane Potomac River bridge built in 1950, connecting Washington, D.C., and Arlington. The 114-million-dollar design-build project commissioned by the District Department of Transportation is being led by Skanska USA Civil, alongside partner firms AECOM and Genesis Structures. Scheduled for completion in the fall of 2029, the initiative aims to extend the structure's operational lifespan by 75 years. The scope of work includes replacing the bascule piers' vessel protection system, updating bridge barriers to meet modern collision standards, rehabilitating the approach spans' superstructure and substructure, and replacing secondary drainage components. Carrying approximately 90,000 motorists daily, the project will convert the existing 175-foot-long bascule span into a fixed span using accelerated bridge construction techniques. The replacement span will be constructed adjacent to the existing structure and maneuvered into position during a 56-hour weekend shutdown. Jointly funded by the Federal Highway Administration and DDOT, the endeavor focuses on enhancing structural resilience. Previously renamed in memory of Arland D. Williams, Jr. following a tragic 1982 aviation incident, the bridge remains a vital component of the regional transportation corridor.
articles.originalTitle: Skanska To Lead Rehab of Landmark Potomac River Bridge - Engineering News-Record

articles.title: Tolu Coker Explores Social Mobility and Identity in Her New London Collection
articles.excerpt: The designer addresses the psychological transition between working-class roots and luxury spaces through a hotel presentation exploring institutional femininity.
articles.content: Tolu Coker presented her Spring 2027 Ready-to-Wear collection through an expansive presentation staged across the upper floors of a London hotel complex. The designer explained that the collection reflects the theme of social mobility and the personal journey of transitioning from working-class roots into institutional and luxury spaces. Building upon previous explorations of her upbringing on a West London council estate, this season's garments and setting examined the psychological nuances of confidence, detachment, and belonging when entering new environments. The presentation space was curated to resemble a lived-in residential interior complete with family photographs and annotated moodboards. The collection featured relaxed iterations of Coker's signature structured tailoring, including looser barrel-leg jeans and paneled jackets. A grounded palette of browns and ecrus was punctuated by accents of cobalt and coral, while new gossamer chiffon blouses and structured dresses introduced a delicate femininity. Alongside the garments, the presentation incorporated chamber orchestra music and exhibited objects, reflecting the designer's comprehensive approach to spatial and emotional storytelling.
articles.originalTitle: Tolu Coker Spring 2027 Ready-to-Wear Collection - Vogue

articles.title: The Gallery House in Pristina Conceived as a Continuous Spatial Experience
articles.excerpt: Designed by Maden Architects in Pristina, Kosovo, The Gallery House integrates architecture, natural light, and landscape into a serene residential experience.
articles.content: Realized in Pristina, Kosovo, The Gallery House brings together architecture, natural light, movement, and landscape to establish a calm and refined residential living experience. Designed by Maden Architects, the project is inspired by the notion of architecture as a continuous journey rather than an aggregation of disconnected spaces. Clean geometric volumes articulate a robust architectural identity, while carefully framed openings, courtyards, and landscaped zones foster a continuous visual and spatial dialogue between the interior and its natural surroundings. The design team implements a planning strategy aimed at fluid spatial transitions for the inhabitants. This holistic approach, perceptible throughout the residence, redefines the relationship between contemporary residential architecture and its environment. Material selections and the calibrated entry of daylight reinforce the project's serene atmosphere, culminating in a balanced aesthetic.

articles.title: Vogue World Milan Celebrates Italian Artisanal Heritage and Fashion History
articles.excerpt: Held in the Galleria, the event honors Italian craftsmanship with runway designs reflecting the Renaissance, Industrial Revolution, and La Dolce Vita eras.
articles.content: Staged in the Galleria in the heart of Milan, the Vogue World event brought together Italy's enduring history of artisanal craft, cutting-edge textile technology, and special collaborations. Francesca Ragazzi, head of editorial content for Vogue Italia, stated that celebrating the story of Made in Italy with a global audience is particularly meaningful in the era of artificial intelligence. Creative director Juan Costa Paz noted that the showcase expresses Italy's leadership in craft through fashion. Opening the presentation, a curated trio featuring a fretwork-crafted scale model of the Duomo, a handmade celestial globe, and a historical loom highlighted the union of hand and machine before the industrial era. The first act celebrated the artisanal revolution, followed by the second act inspired by the industrial manufacturing heritage of Turin, and the third act evoking the cinematic mythology of La Dolce Vita and Italian divas. Showcasing archival pieces from designers like Roberto Capucci and Romeo Gigli alongside tailoring references to Giorgio Armani and Prada, the event traced the evolution of Italian style. Artisans representing various Italian houses participated in the presentation, honoring the country's profound cultural heritage and distinct regional identities.

articles.title: Grand Palais Exhibition in Paris Examines Paul Cezanne's Enduring Influence Across Generations
articles.excerpt: A comprehensive exhibition at the Grand Palais in Paris explores the enduring impact of Paul Cezanne's works on contemporary artists and subsequent generations, including Pablo Picasso and Peter Doig.
articles.content: The Grand Palais in Paris is hosting a major exhibition dedicated to Paul Cezanne, organized through a collaborative partnership between the Centre Pompidou, the Musée d'Orsay, and the Musée de l'Orangerie. Rather than a standard retrospective, the exhibition examines the French master's profound impact on artists who knew him as well as subsequent generations of painters. Curated by Musée d'Orsay paintings curator Jean-Rémi Touzet, the presentation features dozens of works by Cezanne alongside pieces by diverse figures such as André Derain, Wolfgang Tillmans, Joan Mitchell, Zao Wou-Ki, and Etel Adnan. The narrative moves chronologically and thematically through core leitmotifs including landscapes, still lifes, and depictions of bathers, while tracing how modernism was shaped by his abstraction of reality. Highlights include significant loans such as The Bather from the Museum of Modern Art in New York, displayed in dialogue with contemporary responses. Titled Cezanne and Us, the exhibition is hosted at the Grand Palais in Paris.
articles.originalTitle: Paul Cezanne’s influence on generations of artists laid bare in Parisian exhibition - The Art Newspaper

articles.title: New Details Revealed About the Life and Mysterious Works of Claudia del Bufalo
articles.excerpt: Research ahead of an Oslo exhibition sheds fresh light on the 17th-century painter Claudia del Bufalo, long known only for a single portrait and previously assumed to be male. New findings reveal her literary pursuits and mention in a historical murder trial.
articles.content: Research completed ahead of an upcoming exhibition at the National Museum in Oslo has brought to light new details regarding the 17th-century painter Claudia del Bufalo, who has long been recognized primarily for a single documented portrait. For centuries, her signed works were attributed to a male counterpart due to assumptions surrounding the signature. Recent archival investigations conducted by researchers indicate that the artist lived in Rome, working as a professional painter, poet, and theatrical impresario, rather than belonging to the prominent noble family whose name she shared. Court documents from the period suggest her involvement in legal proceedings related to a historical murder case in Rome. Family inventories analyzed by specialists further point to the existence of additional missing paintings attributed to her hand. The exhibition in Oslo features works by women painters from Northern Europe and Italy active between 1550 and 1650, placing her alongside contemporaries through meticulous scholarly cataloging. Curators note that ongoing technical analysis and restoration work on various pieces included in the exhibition continue to refine historical attributions and deepen the understanding of early modern women artists within the broader context of European art history.
articles.originalTitle: From a murder case to hidden works: new details about mysterious 17th-century painter Claudia del Bufalo revealed - The Art Newspaper

articles.title: Kanva Designs a Mass-Timber Museum in Quebec to House Cast-Iron Artifacts
articles.excerpt: Designed by Kanva in Quebec, the Parc Marie-Victorin Museum showcases a vast collection of cast-iron artifacts within subterranean mass-timber pavilions.
articles.content: Designed by architectural firm Kanva in Quebec, Canada, the Parc Marie-Victorin Museum houses an extensive collection of industrial cast-iron artifacts. Created for Alain Lemaire's collection, the project comprises a pair of partially subterranean pavilions that translate the extraction and casting of iron into a spatial narrative. Kanva anchored the volumes around a cluster of mature conifers, establishing a direct relationship with the site's ecology. The green-roofed buildings and charred exterior facades recall the intense heat of the forge while maintaining a dialogue with the landscape. Inside the galleries, exposed cross-laminated timber panels and glulam beams celebrate structural logic without resorting to monumental excess. The visitor circulation sequence mimics the physical sensation of entering and emerging from a mold. Furthermore, a reconstructed historic barn on the premises functions as an active restoration workshop and event venue. The overall design articulates a restrained and tactile architectural language that aligns with the modest spirit of the collection.
articles.originalTitle: A Mass-Timber Museum in Quebec Showcases Cast-Iron Artifacts - architecturalrecord.com

articles.title: New Underwater Habitat Installed Off Florida Keys Sets Precedent for Future Marine Projects
articles.excerpt: Installed off the Florida Keys by international ocean engineering firm DEEP, the four-person Vanguard underwater research habitat enables scientists to conduct deeper-water research while serving as a pilot structure for larger, modular future projects.
articles.content: International ocean engineering and technology company DEEP has deployed a new underwater research habitat at a depth of approximately 60 feet within the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary. Named Vanguard, the four-person structure is designed as a pilot structure and testing ground for more ambitious, modular underwater projects. Prior to installation, comprehensive bathymetric, geotechnical, and biological surveys were conducted to map the seabed, analyze soil composition, and protect local marine life. The primary hull consists of a high-strength steel cylinder adapted from an industrial decompression chamber, serving as living quarters, a workspace, and a decompression facility for saturation diving crews. A steel wet porch bolted to the cylinder features a moon pool enabling divers to enter and exit the facility with ease. Secured to the seabed by a 220-ton base plate and steel piles driven into underlying limestone, the habitat has been engineered to withstand severe hydrodynamic forces and extreme storm conditions. Connected to a surface support buoy via umbilical lines for power, oxygen, and communications, the facility is undergoing commissioning by DNV. Scheduled to host researchers later this year, the habitat will be remotely monitored 24 hours a day from an onshore facility.
articles.originalTitle: Underwater habitat off Florida Keys sets stage for more ambitious projects - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)
